proposed_widenings.name: convert_save_failure_to_success
proposed_widenings.justification: Resist Enchantment allows the bearer to retroactively convert a just-failed saving throw into a success. No existing atom models this. It is distinct from modify_roll_advantage (which gives advantage on future rolls) and from any existing post-roll modifier. The effect fires after the die roll is resolved but before the failed-save consequences apply.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you fail a saving throw against an Enchantment spell that targets only you, you can turn your failed save into a successful one.

proposed_widenings.name: PassiveMechanics.resource (charge_pool)
proposed_widenings.justification: The Cast Spell and Reflect Enchantment properties share a single 10-charge pool. The current surface has no way to declare a shared charge pool across composite components. Each ActivationResource-bearing component must redundantly declare the same pool, which misrepresents the shared depletion constraint. PassiveMechanics also cannot declare a charge pool, forcing charge-cast grants into ActivatedAbilityMechanics even when the activation cost is just 'spend the action to cast'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This staff has 10 charges. [Cast Spell] expend 1 charge... [Reflect Enchantment] expend 1 charge from the staff.

notes: Partial encoding: Cast Spell (3 spells, 1 charge each) and Reflect Enchantment (reaction after save success, 1 charge, reflect_triggering_spell) are encoded cleanly. Resist Enchantment is OMITTED because 'turn a failed save into a success' requires a new atom not in v4. The encoded composite has two components each declaring a charge_pool of cap 10 with dawn reset — this is a surface limitation (no cross-component pool sharing); both declarations represent the same physical pool. The trace and typecheck both pass for the encoded subset.
